Article Title: ‘Utterly shameful’: Tharoor slams police action against women protesters in Delhi
Article Text:
Tharoor condemns alleged police violence against women protesters

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Sunday criticised the alleged police action against women protesters in Delhi, saying it was “utterly shameful” that women protesting violence against women had themselves become victims of violence by policemen.“It’s utterly shameful for women protesting violence against women to become victims of violence against women by policemen!!” Tharoor said in a post on X, while sharing a video student leader by Neha Bora.In the video, Bora announced a citizens’ march from India Gate to Jantar Mantar at 3 pm on Sunday, October 4, calling for protests against the Delhi Police and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Tomorrow 3 PM. From Streets to Protests, Women Are NOT SAFE! Delhi Police's assault against women protestors, journalists will not be tolerated! In the spirit of women taking back the streets: Rise against Delhi Police! Rise against anti-women SIR! Rise for freedom. Rise against Gyanesh Kumar! Citizens' March. India Gate to Jantar Mantar 3 PM, Sunday, 4th October 2026 Jantar Mantar 2.0!”This comes as three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3, with their complaints transferred to the Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial enquiry”.The allegations have drawn criticism from journalists and opposition leaders, with the Committee to Protect Journalists (CJP) set to protest over the incident.AAP Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj and party workers also staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station, demanding registration of an FIR.One of the journalists told PTI that an assistant commissioner of police sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She alleged that police personnel were detaining protesters and that no women police personnel were present at the spot.“Police personnel were detaining protesters, and there were no women police personnel present at the spot. I asked ACP Vivek Bhagat of the Delhi Police about the absence of women police personnel, following which he sexually assaulted me and pushed me back,” she alleged.The journalist said she and others later went to a police station to lodge an FIR but alleged that no action had been taken so far.Delhi Police, however, said on Sunday that it had received complaints from three women journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel.“On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints,” Delhi Police said in a post on X.The complaints were received by the New Delhi district police following the protest, during which police personnel were deployed to maintain law and order. The complaints against the police officers have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market, which will examine the allegations and record statements of the complainants and others concerned.
Article Summary: Congress leader condemns alleged police action against women protesters in Delhi. Tharoor says it is ‘utterly shameful’ that women protesting violence against women had themselves become victims of violence by policemen. Three women journalists have alleged sexual harassment by police personnel while covering a protest.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday said Mahatma Gandhi , Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar and Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru represented three distinct pillars of India’s political and social legacy.In a video post, Dipke described Gandhi as the “SOUL of India”, Ambedkar as the “BACKBONE of India” and Nehru as the “MIND of India”, adding, “You can never become like them.”The development comes as the CJP, led by founder Dipke, organised a protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park on Friday, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.Coinciding with Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary, the protest stage displayed quotations on non-violence and simplicity, alongside tributes to Babasaheb Ambedkar.Mumbai Police have registered an FIR against the organisers and 400-500 unidentified persons in connection with the protest at Shivaji Park.The case has been registered under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Maharashtra Police Act for unlawful assembly, wilful disobedience of a lawful order issued by a public servant and other offences, a Shivaji Park police station official said.The FIR was registered based on a complaint filed by a resident of the Shivaji Park area, the official added.Dipke on Friday night also announced a fresh protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar did not resign.“If Gyanesh Kumar doesn't resign, cockroaches from across India will march to Delhi & protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10,” he said in a post on X, adding that the protest would be peaceful and urging every citizen who wants free and fair elections to join it.

Article Title: ‘If you manufacture a dictator, we will bury it’: Uddhav, Raj launch joint protest against CEC
Article Text:
‘Make in India’ cannot mean manufacturing a dictator, says Uddhav Thackeray

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a joint protest march in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with participants demanding the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra.Addressing the gathering after the march, Uddhav Thackeray accused the government of attempting to create a dictatorship under the slogan of “Make in India”.“I think you will also remember that when Modi ji first became Prime Minister, he gave the slogan, “Make in India.” Remember? We accept that. But if, under “Make in India,” you are also going to manufacture a dictator in our country, then we have gathered here today to bury that dictatorship and put an end to it. Everything else under Make in India is fine. But if, in the name of Make in India, you are going to create a dictatorship, then consider that we have buried your dictatorship. ..”Speaking ahead of the protest, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said the demonstration was a collective response to what he alleged were attempts to undermine democratic institutions, electoral processes and the constitutional rights of citizens.“This protest is against the Hitler-rule prevailing in the country, hijacking elections, keeping the Election Commission and the Supreme Court in one's pocket, running a dictatorship, stealing votes, stealing elections, and poaching MPs and MLAs. This is a revolt against all that, much like the one in 1857,” he told reporters.Thackeray questioned the appointment process of Election Commissioners.“I have a question mark over the appointment of the Election Commissioners. The Election Commission should be appointed through an election. Earlier, there was a committee comprising the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. They (the central government) removed the Chief Justice from this committee. In place of the Chief Justice, they appointed a minister chosen by the Prime Minister. That minister is Amit Shah. There are hearings after hearings in the courts, but there is no accountability.”Thackeray also questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was appointed and alleged that powers related to citizenship rights were being exercised through the Election Commission.“The first question is: How was Gyanesh Kumar appointed? Does the Home Ministry have the power to cancel a person's citizenship rights? They are using that power through Gyanesh Kumar, and that is why we do not want Gyanesh Kumar. Earlier, it was 'India Against Corruption', and now it is 'India Against Vote Chors'... The BJP does not know how to run a government... The way you are running the government is not governance; it is revenge. ..”The march, dubbed the Virat Garjana Morcha (Grand Roar March), began at Metro Cinema and proceeded towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters in south Mumbai. State leaders of the Congress and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) also participated in the protest.The protesters demanded the removal or resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.Party flags were not allowed during the march, with participants and supporters asked to carry only the national tricolour.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray leads protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Participants demand cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra. Thackerays accuses government of attempting to create a dictatorship under the slogan of ‘Make in India’

NEW DELHI: Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan has strongly condemned CPM leader P Nandakumar’s alleged remarks describing Malappuram district as a “nest of fundamentalists and communalists”.In a post on X, Satheesan said the remarks were particularly concerning as they were made in the presence of CPM leader and former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan , without any objection from him. “Strongly condemn the communal slurs made by CPM leader P. NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social media influencer Mad Sandhu, alleging that the state’s law and order was in the hands of the “mafia”.Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Police said the attackers opened fire before fleeing the spot.Sandhu suffered two gunshot wounds and was rushed to a private hospital in critical condition, where he later died during treatment. An eyewitness said around two to three rounds were fired and that Sandhu was shot at close range.Reacting to the killing, Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in Punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.“There is no law and order in Punjab. The law and order situation in Punjab is in the hands of the mafia. In Punjab, you receive only one piece of information every day,” Sirsa told ANI.“Otherwise, the police do not even register an FIR. If they are drug dealers, they are going around killing people. If they are mafia members, they are killing people. If there are gangsters, they are killing people. Social media influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead and if even the Sarpanch of a village is not safe, and a former Sarpanch is not safe, then who is safe?”Sirsa further alleged that extortion gangs, mafia groups and the drug mafia were operating in Punjab.“During the tenure of the Aam Aadmi Party, gangs involved in extortion, the mafia, and the drug mafia are operating in Punjab. There is also a school mafia operating, where even if you raise your voice against problems in schools, you will be thrown out of the party,” he added.Madhusudan Sandhu was a makeup artist and social media influencer who regularly appeared on podcasts and digital platforms, where he spoke about make-up artistry, the film industry and gender issues. His content and fashion choices had also attracted criticism and abuse on social media.Sandhu had around 2.26 lakh followers on Instagram and had acted in the Punjabi film *Oye Bhole Oye*. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had objected to his social media content and clothing, saying his videos could have a negative impact on young people.Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka also criticised the AAP government over the killing and demanded Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, alleging that the government had failed to protect people.Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them publicly on social media. He questioned why the threats had not been taken seriously and demanded an early arrest and a thorough investigation into who was behind the killing and why Sandhu had been threatened.
Article Summary: Madhusudan Sandhu was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa hit out at the Punjab government over the killing. Sirsa alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.

Article Title: ‘Crushing democracy in their DNA’: Shivraj on Congress demanding return to ballot papers
Article Text:
Shivraj questions Congress over disrespecting democracy

Congress demands ballot paper

NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has accused the Congress of disrespecting the public mandate after electoral defeats, alleging that questioning the Election Commission and demanding ballot-paper voting reflected the party’s “DNA”.Chouhan said that while the Congress accepts the Election Commission when it wins elections, it questions the poll body when it loses. Referring to the party’s victories in Karnataka, Telangana and Himachal Pradesh, he asked why the Congress had not raised similar concerns then.While speaking to the reporters on Sunday, he also criticised Congress leaders for demanding a return to ballot-paper voting, recalling allegations of booth capturing and ballot-paper manipulation during the 1980s and 1990s.“Why does the Congress oppose technology that ensures transparent electoral processes?” Chouhan said, accusing the party of trying to undermine democratic institutions.He also invoked the Emergency, alleging that the Congress had weakened democracy in the past and was repeating the same approach.The remarks came a day after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called for the dissolution of the Lok Sabha and all state assemblies, alleging that the elections that brought the current governments to power were “illegal”.He also demanded fresh elections using ballot papers.“Today, the entire country is being run on illegal elections. Modi is an illegal Prime Minister, Shah is an illegal minister, and all the chief ministers who have been elected anywhere are illegal. All of them should be dissolved, elections should be held, and elections should be conducted through ballot papers,” Kharge told reporters in Kalaburagi, Karnataka, on Saturday.
Article Summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan accuses Congress of disrespecting the public mandate after electoral defeats. He asks why the Congress had not raised similar concerns when it won elections. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called for the dissolution of the Lok Sabha and all state assemblies.

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi has alleged that BJP and Sangh Parivar members are attempting to get voters’ names deleted from electoral rolls by filing Form 7, and urged the Election Commission to act against those responsible.Owaisi said printed Form 7 applications were being submitted with the name of the voter sought to be deleted, while the name and details of the person filing the form were not provided.“BJP and Sangh Parivar people are trying to get names deleted by filing Form 7. Printed Form 7 are being submitted where the name of the person whose name is to be deleted is mentioned, but the name and details of the person filing the form are not being provided. If this is happening, it is completely wrong. We are asking the Election Commission of India to take note of this. We are also informing the Chief Electoral Officer of Telangana and the District Electoral Officers that this cannot be allowed,” Owaisi said.He also warned that AIMIM would launch protests in Hyderabad if the alleged practice continued.“If false Form 7 are being filed, we appeal to the Election Commission to take action against those responsible.If this drama does not stop, remember: protests bigger than those at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar will take place on the roads and streets of Hyderabad, and it will create a lot of trouble for you... Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen will not remain silent,” he said.Owaisi had on September 9 sought a four-week extension for electors to file claims and objections against the deletion of names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Telangana.He had visited SIR centres in Hyderabad’s Karwan constituency on Tuesday and alleged that notices had been issued to individuals with six or more children. Following his visit, Owaisi appealed to voters who had received notices to approach AIMIM help desks or contact party leaders and workers in their areas for information and support.The Election Commission had on September 7 revised the schedule for the SIR exercise in Telangana. Under the revised schedule, the claims and objections period will end on October 7 instead of September 16, while the final electoral rolls will be published on November 9.
Article Summary: AIMIM president and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi has alleged that BJP and Sangh Parivar members are attempting to get voters’ names deleted from electoral rolls by filing Form 7. He has urged the Election Commission to act against those responsible. He also warned that AIMIM would launch protests in Hyderabad if the alleged practice continued.

Article Title: BJP hits back at Kharge over 'illegal' remark

NEW DELHI: Hitting back at Congress president Kharge for his "illegal" jibe at PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah BJP said Saturday that it is not only an insult to the democratic wisdom of 140 crore Indians but also shows brazen disrespect for the Constitution and a reflection of the opposition's arrogance."Insulting people's mandate is an old characteristic of Congress. Article Title: Agra court grants bail to 6 Cong workers arrested for defacing CEC Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A local court on Saturday granted bail to six Congress workers arrested for allegedly defacing the outer wall of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home in Agra during a protest against alleged manipulation of voter lists.The accused - Mukesh Dhangar, Anil Yadav, Rajesh Kumar, Manoj Gaur, Rajesh Gautam and Pankaj Chaudhary - were granted bail after furnishing surety bonds of Rs 20,000 each, advocate Santosh Dixit, who represented them, said.The six were arrested on September 29 and had been sent to jail following a case registered against them under several provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including those relating to attempt to murder, rioting, wrongful restraint and assault or criminal force against a public servant.Dixit said the police had dropped Section 109(2) of the BNS, relating to attempt to murder, after failing to substantiate the charge in its submissions before the court.In an earlier hearing, the court had directed the police to conduct a detailed investigation into the invocation of Section 109(1), asking them to specify the facts, injuries, medical evidence, eyewitness testimony or other evidence supporting the charge.The court had also directed the investigating officer to complete the probe by October 3 and drop the section if the investigation did not establish the alleged offence.On September 28 protest in which some Congress workers allegedly wrote slogans with black paint on the gate and outer wall of Kumar's residence in the Vijay Nagar area of Agra.Police registered the case at Hariparvat police station on a complaint by a sub-inspector against eight named persons and 15-20 unidentified Congress workers.The other charges in the case include Section 121 of the BNS, relating to voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter a public servant from performing his duty, Section 126 on wrongful restraint and Section 132 on assault or criminal force against a public servant. Provisions relating to rioting, house-trespass, criminal intimidation and intentional insult were also invoked.Congress Agra city president Amit Singh welcomed the bail order and said the party would continue its agitation against Kumar."The serious section imposed by the police has been removed by the court. This is a victory for democracy," Singh said, adding that the Congress would continue its campaign until Kumar resigns as Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: Six Congress workers arrested for allegedly defacing outer wall of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's ancestral home in Agra. Accused - Mukesh Dhangar, Anil Yadav, Rajesh Kumar, Manoj Gaur and Rajesh Gautam - granted bail after furnishing surety bonds of Rs 20,000 each.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Saturday slammed Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah "illegal" and accused the Congress of disrespecting the Constitution.In a statement, the Union minister described the statement an insult to constitutional institutions and electoral mandate of the people."The statement made by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the direction of leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi is yet another example of their frustration, defeatist mindset and the Congress party's longstanding practice of attacking constitutional institutions," Chouhan said in a statement."Kharge calling the Prime Minister and the home minister 'illegal' is an insult to constitutional institutions and the mandate of the people," he said.This comes after Kharge demanded dissolving the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies, saying that all the elections were illegal and even Prime Minister Modi, home minister Amit Shah and chief ministers of all the states were illegal."Today, the entire country is being run on illegal elections. Modi is an illegal Prime Minister, Shah is an illegal minister, and all the chief ministers who have been elected anywhere are illegal.All of them should be dissolved, elections should be held, and elections should be conducted through ballot papers," he said.He alleged that the ongoing SIR of the electoral roll has many irregularities and is undermining democracy, pointing out that the government is making many mistakes in the process.Kharge pointed out that under the new law, if the CEC or our Election Commissioners commit any mistake, "there can be no inquiry against them anywhere -- till death", alleging that this is how they were destroying democracy.Referring to a report by The Indian Express on the SIR, Kharge said that two members of the Election Commission had written to the Chief Election Commissioner 10 and 14 times, respectively, but their letters had no impact."They cannot speak openly outside, but they expressed their views clearly, he said, adding that if such things continue, they can conduct elections arbitrarily."We have to see whether you want to save democracy in this country or destroy it. That is why we called an all-party meeting and asked everyone to launch an agitation. The first agitation started in Delhi," he said.
Article Summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan slammed Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah "illegal" Chouhan described the statement an insult to constitutional institutions and electoral mandate of the people. Kharge demanded dissolving the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore on Saturday described the participation of actor-politician Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the INDIA bloc's Tamil Nadu meeting as a "historic day", saying the party's entry would strengthen the opposition alliance in the state.An INDIA bloc meeting was held at the TNCC office in Chennai under Tagore's leadership, with Congress, TVK, CPM, CPI, VCK, MDMK and IUML participating. The meeting focused on the opposition's demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and its broader campaign over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.According to ANI, TVK was represented at the meeting by party leaders Aadhav Arjuna and Maria Wilson.Addressing reporters after the meeting, Tagore said Vijay-led TVK had joined the INDIA bloc and said its entry would strengthen the bloc in Tamil Nadu."Vijay-led TVK has joined the INDIA alliance. It's a very historic day for the INDIA alliance. The INDIA alliance, particularly in Tamil Nadu, is to be strengthened by the entry of TVK," Tagore said, according to ANI.Tagore also linked the development to the opposition's political contest with the BJP, saying the fight against the BJP and the policies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah would become "interesting" in Tamil Nadu.The meeting also decided to intensify protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Tagore said INDIA bloc parties would hold demonstrations at district headquarters across Tamil Nadu, followed by a joint protest in Chennai on October 15."We have decided to have the district-level demonstrations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. We demand his resignation," Tagore said, adding that the participating parties would release the list of leaders taking part in the demonstrations.He said all seven parties participating in Saturday's meeting would join the Chennai protest on October 15.MDMK general secretary Vaiko said the meeting had welcomed TVK's participation and appreciated the presence of its leader, Vijay. He also announced a series of statewide rallies against the Chief Election Commissioner on October 13, 14 and 15, according to ANI."This meeting has welcomed the decision of the TVK and appreciated the participation of C Joseph Vijay," Vaiko said. He added that the rallies would demand the removal of Gyanesh Kumar from the post of Chief Election Commissioner.TVK's participation in the Tamil Nadu meeting comes amid a broader opposition campaign against the Election Commission over the SIR exercise, electoral rolls and other election-related issues.Top INDIA bloc leaders had met at the Constitution Club on September 30 to discuss alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls, concerns over electronic voting machines and the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Article Summary: Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) joined the INDIA bloc's Tamil Nadu meeting. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore called it a "historic day" He said TVK's entry would strengthen the opposition alliance in the state.

Article Title: Minors used to deter police action at CJP’s Mumbai protest? NHRC seeks report
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Human Rights Commission ( NHRC ) on Saturday issued a notice over the alleged involvement of minors in the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest in Mumbai.The NHRC sought an Action Taken Report on allegations that minors were placed “strategically” at the protest site to deter police from taking action against demonstrators.On Friday, the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, youth pressure group CJP held a protest at Mumbai’s iconic Shivaji Park, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over an alleged rift between him and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Thousands of people, including celebrities such as Naseeruddin Shah, Shabana Azmi, Vishal Bhardwaj and Vishal Dadlani, turned up at Shivaji Park demanding the removal of the CEC.The protest was held despite the Mumbai Police denying permission. The CJP also announced that it would hold a protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar from October 10 if Kumar does not resign or is not removed by then.The CJP had also led youth protests at Jantar Mantar, Delhi’s designated protest venue, in June and July, seeking the resignation or removal of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue.Pradhan resigned on July 25, bringing the agitation to an end.
Article Summary: The National Human Rights Commission issued a notice over the alleged involvement of minors in the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest in Mumbai. The NHRC sought an Action Taken Report on allegations that minors were placed “strategically” at the protest site to deter police from taking action against demonstrators.

Article Title: 12 BJP CMs defend EC amid SIR row, hit back at Rahul Gandhi after poll body's fresh note
Article Text:
BJP CMs Rekha Gupta, Devendra Fadnavis and Yogi Adityanath

What BJP CMs said

Rahul Gandhi’s cryptic post

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The controversy

NEW DELHI: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday, a day after the Election Commission of India (ECI) issued a press release responding to a media report that had claimed a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.According to a statement issued by the ruling party, the chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions."In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis remarked that "no vote was stolen, Rahul Gandhi's mind was stolen." He accused the Lok Sabha leader of opposition of "seeking to spread anarchy by defaming institutions" while claiming to defend the Constitution.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused the opposition parties of creating "confusion" over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma described the INDIA bloc as an “alliance of losers,” while Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary argued that "cleansing" the voter list was necessary because “booth capturing no longer works in the country.”West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari pointed to the Congress’s support for the SIR in Keralam, where it won, and its opposition to the exercise in Bengal after losing the election.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami objected to what he described as an "attempt to defame institutions by presenting a note from an internal discussion as a final decision.”Rajasthan chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma questioned why the Congress had not "verified the facts" before making serious allegations over the June 24, 2025, orders concerning the nationwide SIR, which he maintained were adopted by the ECI full consensus of the CEC and the election commissioners.Chhattisgarh's Vishnu Deo Sai accused the Congress of resorting to “anti-national” conduct after “having lost more than 100 elections.” Referring to the Election Commissioners’ joint statement, accompanied by a photograph of the three officials seated at a table, Sai argued that it had exposed what he called a “conspiracy to tarnish the country’s image.”Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, where a third of the electorate was removed and a third of those remaining received notices as part of the ongoing revision, framed the Opposition’s position on the issue as an attempt to “divert attention from its failures."Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, posted cryptically on X: “I love swimming in the sea when it’s rough. It teaches you that rough is just another kind of calm.”At a press conference on September 24, a day after The Indian Express published its report, the Congress leader claimed his “vote chori” (vote theft) allegation stood “vindicated.” The Raebareli MP also demanded that CEC Gyanesh Kumar resign or be removed, accusing him of “treason.”The Indian Express reported on September 23 that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to at least 14 decisions over 10 months concerning the ongoing SIR exercise and related matters.The ECI has not disputed that objections were raised; however it characterised them as "disagreements" that were subsequently resolved, stressing that the final decisions were "unanimous." While Sandhu and Joshi are yet to speak to the media, the poll panel's press note second statement outlined several measures and clarifications.The BJP has maintained that the ECI’s press notes have “settled the matter”. Its allies, who, like the opposition, had sought an explanation from the poll body, also welcomed the commission's statement.
Article Summary: A dozen BJP chief ministers held press conferences in their respective states on Sunday. The chief ministers accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and his party-led opposition INDIA bloc of “conspiring to defame constitutional institutions” In states where the BJP or its NDA allies are not in power, state BJP presidents or leaders of the opposition from the saffron party addressed media instead.

Article Title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
Article Text:
The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.





CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. Multiple raids were also conducted at his residence, relatives houses and other possible locations.A petition was filed before the Punjab and Haryana high court seeking transfer of the investigation to the CBI or another independent agency, alleging that Gulzar Singh had faced intimidation and that his video statement contained allegations against certain persons.
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.

Article Title: FIR on CJP for unlawful assembly, traffic disruption at Shivaji Park stir in Mumbai
Article Text:
An FIR has been lodged against the Cockroach Janta Party after their protest at Shivaji Park





MUMBAI: Police registered an FIR against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) for allegedly holding an unlawful assembly, raising slogans, disrupting the smooth flow of traffic and using loudspeakers without permission during a protest at Shivaji Park on Friday.CJP supporters were protesting, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over concerns surrounding Election Commission and SIR.According to the FIR, around 400 to 500 unidentified supporters and protesters, including CJP members Ajinkya Shinde, Pranay Ahire, Ashutosh Ranka, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Afreen Nawaz, Soumya Korde, Ankit Bhardwaj, Vijay Malangi and Yogesh Ingale, gathered at the protest venue at 2 pm and stayed put until 7 pm.According to the FIR, the protesters gathered on a public road, allegedly obstructed traffic and raised slogans, leading to a law-and-order situation. Police also alleged that loudspeakers were used to address the gathering without the required permission.The FIR has been registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including those relating to unlawful assembly and disobedience of a lawful order, along with provisions of the Maharashtra Police Act.CJP organised a ‘Jail Bharo’ protest on Friday, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, amid reports of differences within Election Commission.Despite heavy police deployment and denial of formal permission for the protest at Shivaji Park, a large number of citizens and supporters gathered at the venue.Meanwhile, Shivaji Park resident and advocate Siddhi Deolekar too filed a police complaint against Abhijeet Dipke and others, alleging illegal gathering and protest.Deolekar said she lodged the complaint against Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ratna Singh, alleging that they proceeded with the protest and attempted to gather a large crowd despite not having any required permissions.
Article Summary: CJP supporters were protesting, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over concerns surrounding Election Commission and SIR. According to the FIR, around 400 to 500 unidentified supporters and protesters, including CJP members gathered at the protest venue at 2 pm and stayed put until 7 pm.

Article Title: Baby Indian rock python rescued from sea by Mumbai police
Article Text: Mumbai: A patrolling boat of the Mumbai Police spotted an Indian rock python struggling in the sea, after which they decided to intervene and rescue it.Soon after safely securing the snake in the boat, they contacted RAWW (Resqink Association for Wildlife Welfare) for further assistance in its medical examination and rehabilitation in coordination with State Forest Department.The baby python of around 2 feet in length was brought back to the coast and handed over to the rescuer Rahul Bhosle from RAWW. It was then examined by Dr Priti Sathe from RAWW and provided with necessary medical intervention.After keeping it under observation for 12 hours, it was released back to its natural habitat in coordination with Mumbai Territorial Wing of Forest Department.Names of the compassionate cops who helped in the python rescue are ASI Sachin Bhagwan Tandel, ASI Pandurang Dattatray Gaware, police constable Nilesh Narayan Malusare, and police constable Vijay Dilip More.Previously, a similar coastal police unit helped in rescuing a loggerhead sea turtle as well.
Article Summary: The baby python of around 2 feet in length was brought back to the coast and handed over to the rescuer. It was then examined by Dr Priti Sathe from RAWW and provided with necessary medical intervention. After keeping it under observation for 12 hours, it was released back to its natural habitat.

Article Title: ​​Unrest within BJP as Bawankule hints at offering Aurangabad division graduates’ poll seat to NCP
Article Text:
Sitting MLC Satish Chavan has already started his campaign for ​​Aurangabad Division Graduates’ constituency poll

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Several BJP politicains have been feeling unsettled since revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule hinted at giving up the party’s claim over Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency poll on Friday.Bawankule said that Mahayuti has decided that the seat won by the party in the grand alliance would remain with the same party, indicating that NCP would have a claim over the seat.While no official announcement of the candidate has been made yet from the Mahayuti camp, sitting MLC of Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency, Satish Chavan has already started his poll campaign.The comment made by Bawankule, which reflected a larger understanding of top leaders from BJP-NCP, has produced unrest as well as gloom within the BJP camp as its leaders were trying hard to wrest the seat from NCP.“We have left no stone unturned to ensure maximum voter registration for the upcoming MLC poll with the hope of a BJP candidate getting a ticket. We have already paid multiple visits to top leaders to convey our sentiments. Despite hints from Bawankule, we hope for a miracle to happen at the last moment,” a BJP leader from Marathwada said.The BJP camp from Marathwada had repeatedly raised the fact that Chavan had unsuccessfully contested the 2024 assembly poll from Gangapur against Mahayuti.Gangapur BJP MLA Prashant Bamb was among the party leaders who were openly opposing a Mahayuti ticket to Chavan.If the BJP gives up its claim, it will be the first time in the history that the the party will not be in the fray for the Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency poll.On Saturday, a total of 31 aspirants collected 59 nomination forms for ​Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency poll, and ten candidates filed their papers. So far, 174 forms have been issued to 97 aspirants and 12 candidates have filed nominations, according to official data.
Article Summary: Several BJP politicains have been feeling unsettled since revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule hinted at giving up the party’s claim over Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency poll. No official announcement of the candidate has been made yet from the Mahayuti camp.

Article Title: Bhaiyya Mane breaks with Mushrif, NCP over Pune Graduate seat
Article Text:
Kolhapur





:District Cooperative Bank director Pratap Mane, popularly known as ‘Bhaiyya Mane’, has parted ways with minister Hasan Mushrif and the NCP amid uncertainty in Mahayuti over the nomination for the Pune Graduate constituency.Mane, a long-time supporter of Mushrif, has decided to contest the election irrespective of whether he gets the party nomination. He became emotional while announcing his decision.Mushrif on Saturday said, “Mane had undertaken substantial voter-registration work over the past five years and NCP had sought the nomination for him. However, NCP MLC Arun Lad had joined BJP , while CM Fadnavis had assured the candidature to Lad’s son, Sharad Lad, making it likely that the seat would go to BJP.”Mushrif said he had tried to persuade Mane, but the latter asked him not to stand in the way of his political future. “My relationship with Mane has ended. NCP will have to work for Mahayuti as a constituent of the alliance,” he said.Mane, however, said there was no question of withdrawing from the contest as he had been preparing for the election for several years. He also highlighted his role in securing Rs 50 crore for infrastructure development at Shivaji University.Mane acknowledged that NCP might have faced limitations in securing the seat and said the situation could have been different had Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar been alive.Mane’s supporters had earlier expressed displeasure over Mahayuti’s failure to decide its candidate and urged him to contest either on a party ticket or as an independent.Suggestions were also made that Mushrif should submit voter-registration data to senior leaders, allow Mane to contest independently and ask Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar to permit a friendly contest within Mahayuti. With the candidature issue unresolved, Mane eventually left Mushrif’s camp.NCP had won the Pune Graduate seat in the previous election. However, BJP Rajya Sabha MP Dhananjay Mahadik has claimed the seat for BJP following Lad’s switch from NCP. Mahadik has said BJP will contest both the Pune Graduate and Teachers constituencies.Several members of the Shiv Sena factions are also interested in contesting the two constituencies. Their next move remains under scrutiny amid indications that both seats could go to BJP.
Article Summary: Pratap Mane, popularly known as ‘Bhaiyya Mane’, has parted ways with minister Hasan Mushrif and the NCP. NCP MLC Arun Lad had joined BJP, while CM Fadnavis had assured the candidature to Lad’s son, Sharad Lad.

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Three held on charge of robbery
Article Text:
South Mahalunge police arrest two robbers

Pune:





Pimpri Chinchwad police on Thursday arrested two men and detained a minor for allegedly robbing a 29-year-old sugarcane juice vendor of Rs12,000 in Nighoje on Sept 28.The victim was returning home in Mhalunge when he boarded a shared rickshaw at Nigdi bus stop with three men, one of them the driver. The trio threatened him with a sharp weapon, robbed him and dumped him on the road before driving off.Two of the accused, Aman Shaikh (26) and Shekhar Mane (21), have criminal records. Shaikh, arrested earlier under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), was released on bail about 15 days ago. Mane has cases of robbery and assault registered against him.Acting on the victim’s complaint, police traced the autorickshaw and took the trio into custody.“We are investigating whether the duo and their minor accomplice were involved in more crimes,” a police officer said.
Article Summary: Two of the accused, Aman Shaikh (26) and Shekhar Mane (21), have criminal records. Shaikh, arrested earlier under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), was released on bail about 15 days ago. Mane has cases of robbery and assault registered against him.

Article Title: Man held for bludgeoning friend to death
Article Text:
Pune:





The Khadak police on Saturday arrested a 34-year-old man for bludgeoning his friend to death over an argument in Kashewadi in Bhavani Peth.Police said the deceased Akash Patole (30), a roadside vendor, was out with his friends on Friday night when “the accused bludgeoned him with a cement block and fled. Patole was taken to a hospital, where doctors pronounced him dead. ”An officer said while Patole’s sister-in-law came to the police station to lodge a complaint, the accused reached there and surrendered himself. “We have arrested him. Our investigations are on,” he said.The accused, Ajay Shinde alias Chor Raja has been arrested under Section 103 (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Article Summary: Ajay Shinde alias Chor Raja has been arrested under Section 103 (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Police said the deceased Akash Patole (30), a roadside vendor, was out with his friends on Friday night when ‘the accused bludgeoned him with a cement block and fled’

Article Title: Youth assaulted at Jargaon gram sabha after questioning lack of fogging, case against former sarpanch & 2 others
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A question over why a village fogging machine was lying unused allegedly led to the assault of a youth during a special gram sabha at Jargaon in Pachora taluka on Friday.Pachora police registered a case against former sarpanch Sunil Patil and two of his relatives following a complaint by Anand Patil. Police took the two relatives into custody, while the former sarpanch was not traceable.The special Gram Sabha was convened on Gandhi Jayanti to discuss development works, civic amenities and public grievances. During the meeting, Anand raised the growing mosquito menace and questioned why the fogging machine was not being used.Police said this sparked a heated argument between Anand and the former sarpanch, which soon escalated into an alleged physical assault.A video of the altercation later was circulated on social media, triggering outrage in the area.Following Anand’s complaint, Pachora police booked the three under BNS sections 115(2) for voluntarily causing hurt and 352 for intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace.Jargaon police patil Namdeo Patil said Anand owns a house in the village, which has a population of around 15,000.The Jargaon Gram Panchayat is currently being run by an administrator.
Article Summary: A question over why a village fogging machine was lying unused allegedly led to the assault of a youth during a special gram sabha at Jargaon in Pachora taluka on Friday. Police registered a case against former sarpanch Sunil Patil and two of his relatives.

Article Title: TVK moves ECI against Stalin over ‘body-shaming’ remarks on Dharapuram candidate
Article Text:
Move by Aadhav Arjuna and party's legal wing

Chennai:





TVK general secretary (election management) and PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna, along with the party’s legal wing, has approached the Election Commission of India seeking action against DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin for allegedly violating the model code of conduct by making derogatory, body-shaming remarks about TVK’s Dharapuram candidate P Sathyabama.In his complaint, Arjuna urged the ECI to withdraw Stalin’s star campaigner status and direct the district returning officer to register an FIR against him under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, 1998. He also sought measures to ensure Sathyabama’s “fearless participation” in the electoral process.Talking to mediapersons at the Secretariat, Arjuna warned that legal action would be initiated against Stalin and Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin if they continued making derogatory remarks against women. “We respect the DMK leader, but Stalin has increasingly resorted to denigrating women at a level unseen in the past five years. We are planning to file a formal criminal complaint against the DMK chief,” Arjuna said.In a separate representation, the TVK advocates’ wing urged the ECI to immediately direct Stalin to refrain from making such remarks and, if necessary, impose restrictions on his election campaign.The wing sought registration of an FIR under the relevant provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Representation of the People Act. It also called for a lawful investigation and penal action. “The video and audio recordings, along with media reports of the meeting, may be immediately seized and preserved. Details of the action taken on this complaint may be communicated to us,” the representation said.
Article Summary: TVK general secretary (election management) and PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna, along with the party’s legal wing, has approached the Election Commission of India seeking action against DMK president and former chief minister M K Stalin. He is alleged to have made derogatory, body-shaming remarks about TVK's Dharapuram candidate P Sathyabama.

Article Title: FIR against Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving child in poll campaign in Dharapuram
Article Text:
Authorities in Dharapuram have filed a case against Udhayanidhi Stalin for infringing on the Model Code of Conduct during a recent election rally





TIRUPUR: Dharapuram Police have registered a case against Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin for involving a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram, where the Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll.According to a press release issued by Tirupur district police, the incident took place on Saturday near the Periyar statue in Dharapuram town during an election campaign meeting addressed by Udhayanidhi.Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in any election-related activities.Police said Udhayanidhi made a child speak at the campaign meeting in a manner that was insulting to Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and also used the child for election campaigning.Dharapuram Town Police registered a case against Udhayanidhi. Further investigation is under way, police said.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Assembly Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin involved a child in an election campaign meeting at Dharapuram. The Model Code of Conduct is in force for the bypoll. Police said the Election Commission had clearly instructed political parties and candidates not to involve children in election-related activities.

Article Title: Six arrested in Coimbatore for possessing synthetic drug, ganja
Article Text: COIMBATORE: In two separate cases, the Coimbatore city police on Friday arrested six men on charges of possessing synthetic drug methamphetamine and ganja.On Friday evening, the Sundarapuram police seized 58 gram of methamphetamine from three men and arrested them. The arrested men have been identified as B Annamalai, 25, of Kurichi Housing Unit, R Arunpandi, 27, of Madurai and A Gopinath, 21 of Dindigul.Based on specific information about synthetic drug sales, the Sundarapuram police reached Mohan Nagar on the Madukkarai Main Road and began a search. They found the trio under a flyover. Upon checking them, police found 58 grams of methamphetamine in their possession.A case was registered under Section 8(c) read with Section 22(c) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act). They were remanded in judicial custody.In a separate incident, Ukkadam police arrested R Arun, 20 of Sivagangai District, S Bhuvanesh, 22 of Theni and K Raman, 23 of Madurai and seized 3.6 kg of ganja from them. The trio were remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: Coimbatore city police on Friday arrested six men on charges of possessing synthetic drug methamphetamine and ganja. On Friday evening, the Sundarapuram police seized 58 gram of methamphetamine from three men and arrested them. In a separate incident, Ukkadam police arrested R Arun, 20 of Sivagangai District, S Bhuvanesh, 22 of Theni and K Raman, 23 of Madurai.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu’s economy heading towards abyss under Vijay’s TVK govt: BJP
Article Text:
Nainar Nagenthran





COIMBATORE: BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran on Friday alleged that the Tamil Nadu ’s economy has deteriorated under TVK govt and is “heading towards the abyss.” He accused the TVK regime of functioning largely as a “social media govt.”Nagenthran was in Pollachi to pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. Speaking to reporters later, he launched a broadside against TVK govt and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He said that during the first 144 days of TVK govt, around 500 crimes had been reported. He alleged that 30 people associated with the party were accused in rape cases and no action had been taken against them.He said BJP would continue to expand its political presence in Tamil Nadu and claimed that the party would eventually establish its “full authority” in the state.Asked about the bypolls in Dharapuram and Madurantakam, Nagenthran alleged that the resignation of MLAs after getting elected amounted to “horse-trading.” He held chief minister Vijay responsible for this and demanded a judicial inquiry into the alleged horse-trading.Nagenthran stated that the state was facing power shortages and increased power cuts, affecting industrial units. He alleged that govt had failed to introduce adequate welfare and development schemes for the people. “There is no people-oriented governance. There is nothing for the welfare of the people,” he said.
Article Summary: Nainar Nagenthran was in Pollachi to pay floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. He launched a broadside against TVK govt and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He said that 30 people associated with the party were accused in rape cases and no action had been taken.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.

Article Title: Roof collapse at sports meet venue: Keralam child rights panel registers suo motu case
Article Text:
Thrissur

:





Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a suo motu case following media reports that students and parents were injured when the roof of the venue hosting swimming competitions as part of the State School Sports Meet in Thrissur collapsed.Thrissur witnessed a series of protests on Saturday demanding action against officials whose alleged negligence led to the mishap. The protesters, mainly from BJP and DYFI, also demanded the resignation of sports minister and education minister, holding them morally responsible for the alleged official negligence.Opposition and ruling-front councillors came to blows at the Thrissur corporation after opposition members sought to raise the issue at the council meeting.The commission noted that several reports had emerged regarding the difficulties faced by students during the conduct of the sports meet and observed that there had been gross negligence on the part of the organisers. It further noted that the teachers in charge had adopted an irresponsible attitude.Commission member Jalajamol T C said they have sought explanations from director of general education, district police chief, deputy director of education (Thrissur) and district child protection officer.BJP and DYFI workers took out marches to the office of deputy director of education. The police initially removed the BJP workers, while SFI volunteers staged a sit-in, insisting that they be allowed to meet the deputy director. They were also removed by the police later.DYFI also took out a march to the city police commissioner’s office in the evening, demanding the resignation of the two ministers.BJP and LDF councillors alleged that Congress councillors attacked them while they were raising the issue of alleged serious negligence in organising the aquatic competitions.Mayor Niji Justin and deputy mayor Prasad said the corporation had no role in organising the sports event and accused the opposition of attempting to rake up unnecessary issues.
Article Summary: Thrissur witnessed a series of protests on Saturday demanding action against officials whose alleged negligence led to the mishap. The protesters, mainly from BJP and DYFI, also demanded the resignation of sports minister and education minister. Opposition and ruling-front councillors came to blows at the Thrissur corporation.

Article Title: Photographer held with 38g MDMA and over ₹15 lakh in Kochi
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A 34-year-old photographer was arrested with MDMA by Ernakulam Excise special squad on Saturday.Arun K Nair, 34, of Pampady, Kottayam, was travelling in a car when he was arrested at Kakkanad allegedly with 38.13g of MDMA and more than Rs 15 lakh in cash.Deputy excise commissioner P K Satheesh said at a news conference that they have information about Arun supplying drugs to those in the film industry. He mainly sold drugs to youngsters and students.The money was kept in a bag inside the car, in bundles of Rs 3,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 10,000. Drug cartels allegedly supplied him with quantities of 250g, 500g or 1kg at a time. He bought the drugs once every two days. He paid the drug gang only after selling the drugs and retaining his profit, excise said.More arrests are likely in the case. The deputy excise commissioner said the investigation had found that a person named Ubaid, a native of Kozhikode, supplied the drugs to Arun.He sold the MDMA, which was sourced from Delhi and other north Indian states, at Rs 3,000 per gram. The excise department will investigate his financial transactions and phone call records.Meanwhile, an Assam native was arrested with brown sugar. Najar Ali, 30, was taken into custody by Palarivattom Police.He was arrested near a bus stop near Palarivattom Junction. Police seized 1.20g of brown sugar, which had been kept in a zip-lock cover allegedly for sale.Ernakulam Rural police also arrested one more accused in a case involving the seizure of 37kg of ganja. Suman Sheikh, 23, of Murshidabad in West Bengal, was arrested from Olavakkode railway station in Palakkad early on Friday.The ganja was seized on Aug 1 as part of Operation Toofan. Sabuj Sheikh, 19, and Raja Sheikh, natives of Murshidabad, were earlier arrested by Rural district Dansaf team, a special investigation team led by Munambam DSP, and Paravur Police.Suman was arrested with the assistance of the Railway Protection Force. He is alleged to be the person who supplied ganja to those arrested earlier.Woman booked for theft: A case has been registered against a woman from Edappally in connection with the theft of gold ornaments while staying as a paying guest. The allegation is that ornaments worth Rs 1.90 lakh, including a 6.59g gold chain and 6.09g jhumka earrings kept in a locker inside a room, were stolen. Palarivattom police have registered a case.
Article Summary: Arun K Nair, 34, of Pampady, Kottayam, was travelling in a car when he was arrested at Kakkanad allegedly with 38.13g of MDMA and more than Rs 15 lakh in cash. He mainly sold drugs to youngsters and students.
